propositions.text: Applicant is incarcerated at Millhaven Institution in segregation since July 15, 2015.
propositions.quote: The Applicant, Timothy Mitchel Nome, is currently incarcerated at Millhaven Institution, a maximum-security facility located in Ontario, where he has remained in segregation since July 15, 2015.

propositions.text: Applicant commenced judicial review on June 18, 2014, alleging CSC refused access to health treatments.
propositions.quote: On June 18, 2014, he commenced this application for judicial review seeking relief in respect of an alleged refusal by Correctional Service of Canada [CSC], to provide him access to various health treatments and services.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant is incarcerated in segregation at Millhaven since July 2015 and commenced judicial review in June 2014 alleging CSC refused health treatments.

propositions.text: Applicant filed a motion on September 15, 2015, seeking to enjoin transfer out of Ontario pending judicial review.
propositions.quote: In a separate motion filed with the Court on September 15, 2015, the Applicant also sought relief under Rule 373 of the Federal Courts Rules, SOR/98-106, enjoining the Respondents from transferring him out of the Ontario region pending the determination of this application for judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant filed motion to enjoin transfer out of Ontario pending judicial review determination.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is dismissed; interlocutory relief motion need not be decided.
propositions.quote: For the reasons set out below, the application for judicial review is dismissed. As a result, there is no need for this Court to dispose of the motion for interlocutory relief.

paragraphs.summary: Application for judicial review dismissed; interlocutory relief motion not decided.

propositions.text: Applicant was injured in 2011 altercation with CSC officers, suffering broken nose, finger, and chipped teeth.
propositions.quote: On January 27, 2011, while incarcerated at the Special Handling Unit of the Regional Reception Centre in Saint-Anne-des-Plaines, Québec, the Applicant was injured in an altercation with CSC officers. During this incident, the Applicant asserts that he suffered a broken nose, broken finger and two (2) chipped teeth.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant asserts he was injured in 2011 altercation with CSC officers, suffering broken nose, finger, and chipped teeth.

propositions.text: Applicant transferred to four institutions between 2012 and 2013, currently at Millhaven since October 2013.
propositions.quote: Since the incident in 2011, the Applicant has been transferred to four (4) different institutions, including: Kent Institution, British Columbia in March 2012; Mountain Institution, British Columbia in August 2012; Atlantic Institution, New Brunswick in January 2013; and his current location, Millhaven Institution, Ontario in October 2013.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant transferred to four institutions from 2012 to 2013, currently at Millhaven since October 2013.

propositions.text: Applicant requested health treatments including rhinoplasty, dental implants, finger surgery, and new glasses.
propositions.quote: Throughout his incarceration, the Applicant has requested that CSC provide health treatment and services for his aforementioned injuries, including rhinoplasty to reconfigure his nose, replacement of the two (2) teeth with dental implants, surgery to his left hand fifth finger, and a new pair of eye glasses.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant requested health treatments including rhinoplasty, dental implants, finger surgery, and new glasses.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted offender complaint on July 12, 2013, alleging denial of timely healthcare access.
propositions.quote: On July 12, 2013, the Applicant submitted an offender complaint for being denied reasonable and timely access to healthcare (#V20R00005982). Claiming to have been scheduled for surgery in March 2012, before his transfer to Kent Institution, the Applicant requested that he be scheduled for surgery for repairs to his left hand fifth finger and a rhinoplasty procedure for his nose.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submitted offender complaint in July 2013 alleging denial of timely healthcare access and requested surgeries.

propositions.text: Complaint upheld in part; delay acknowledged but medical needs addressed with x-rays and possible specialist referral.
propositions.quote: In a response dated August 8, 2013, the Applicant’s complaint was upheld in part by the Acting Chief of Health Services at Atlantic Institution. The Acting Chief found that there was indeed a delay in receiving services, but noted that the Applicant’s medical needs had been addressed: his nose and left hand fifth finger had been x-rayed on July 31, 2013. The response also indicated that once the results of these x-rays were received, the Applicant would be referred, if required, to specialists.

paragraphs.summary: Complaint upheld in part; delay acknowledged but medical needs addressed with x-rays and possible specialist referral.

propositions.text: Applicant grieved decision on August 22, 2013, maintaining denial of health treatment and requesting transfer for timely surgeries.
propositions.quote: On August 22, 2013, the Applicant grieved this decision to the first level of the grievance process, maintaining that he was still being denied health treatment and services. He indicated that he may be transferred to Ontario and asked whether CSC would fly him back to the Atlantic region so that the surgeries could be done in a timely manner.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant grieved decision in August 2013, maintaining denial of treatment and requesting transfer for surgeries.

propositions.text: First level grievance upheld in part; initial x-ray delay acknowledged; transfer flight request denied as beyond authority.
propositions.quote: In a response dated November 1, 2013, the first level grievance was upheld in part, again on the basis that there was an initial delay in having x-rays completed. With respect to the Applicant’s request that he be flown back to the Atlantic region for treatment, the response indicated that this request was beyond the authority of CSC Health Services.

paragraphs.summary: First level grievance upheld in part; initial x-ray delay acknowledged; transfer flight request denied as beyond authority.

propositions.text: Applicant commenced judicial review application on June 18, 2014.
propositions.quote: On June 18, 2014, the Applicant commenced this application for judicial review.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant commenced judicial review application on June 18, 2014.

propositions.text: Applicant submitted final level grievance on September 6, 2015, regarding delays in requested health treatments; decision pending.
propositions.quote: On September 6, 2015, the Applicant submitted a final level grievance with respect to the delays in obtaining his requested health treatment and services, namely, rhinoplasty surgery, surgery to his left hand fifth finger, dental implants, and proper fitting eye glasses. A final level grievance decision remains pending.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant submitted final grievance in September 2015 about treatment delays; decision pending.

propositions.text: Notice of Involuntary Transfer Recommendation issued September 15, 2015, recommending transfer to Stony Mountain Institution to alleviate segregation.
propositions.quote: On September 15, 2015, a Notice of Involuntary Transfer Recommendation was issued, recommending that the Applicant be transferred to Stony Mountain Institution, Manitoba. The Applicant was advised that the transfer was recommended to alleviate his segregation status and to provide him with a safe environment in which to reside, considering that attempts to integrate the Applicant into the prison population had been unsuccessful.

paragraphs.summary: Notice recommending transfer to Stony Mountain issued September 2015 to alleviate segregation and provide safe environment.

propositions.text: Transfer decision finalized October 16, 2015, communicated to Applicant October 28, 2015.
propositions.quote: The decision to transfer the Applicant from Millhaven Institution to Stony Mountain Institution was finalized on October 16, 2015, and communicated to the Applicant on October 28, 2015.

paragraphs.summary: Transfer decision finalized October 16, 2015, and communicated October 28, 2015.

propositions.text: Issues: exhaustion of remedies and compelling circumstances; mootness; CSC's reasonable response to health requests and remedy.
propositions.quote: Having considered the submissions of the parties, the following issues arise from this application for judicial review: A. Has the Applicant exhausted his alternative remedies and if not, are there compelling circumstances such that this Court should entertain the application for judicial review? B. Is the application for judicial review moot? C. Did CSC reasonably address the Applicant’s requests for health treatment and services? If not, what is the appropriate remedy?

paragraphs.summary: Issues: exhaustion of remedies and compelling circumstances; mootness; CSC's reasonable response and remedy.

propositions.text: Preliminary issue: underlying matter and relief sought by Applicant.
propositions.quote: Before addressing the above-noted issues, a preliminary issue arises as to what the underlying matter consists of and what relief is being sought by the Applicant.

propositions.text: Applicant seeks judicial review quashing CSC decision denying health treatments, Charter and CCRA breaches, and immediate treatment.
propositions.quote: In his Notice of Application filed June 18, 2014, the Applicant indicates that he is seeking judicial review of the “decision of the [CSC] on or about June 10, 2014 continuing to deny him access to needed health service treatments that they had undertaken would be implemented many months ago”. Specifically, he seeks the following: A. an order in the nature of certiorari quashing the Respondent Commissioner’s decision to continually refuse to provide the Applicant’s needed evaluations and treatments; B. an order declaring that the Respondents have acted contrary to section 7 of the Canadian Charter of Rights and Freedoms, Part I of the Constitution Act, 1982, Schedule B to the Canada Act 1982 (UK), 1982, c 11 [Charter]; C. an order declaring that the Respondents breached their obligations under the Corrections and Conditional Release Act, SC 1992, c 20 [CCRA] and in particular its health services obligations under sections 85 to 87 thereof, as well as its obligation to provide safe and healthful custody under section 70 thereof; and, D. an order requiring the Respondents to provide the Applicant his health service evaluations and treatments immediately.

paragraphs.summary: Preliminary issue: Applicant seeks judicial review quashing CSC denial, Charter and CCRA breaches, and immediate treatment.

propositions.text: Applicant's November 27, 2015 memorandum seeks to quash transfer decision and prevent transfer until health services accessed.
propositions.quote: In light of his pending transfer to Manitoba, the Applicant has included in his Memorandum of Fact and Law, filed November 27, 2015, request for relief which is appreciably different than the relief sought in the Notice of Application. The Applicant now seeks the following in his Memorandum of Fact and Law: A. an order quashing the decision of the Warden, on October 15, 2015, to involuntarily transfer the Applicant to Stony Mountain Institution; B. an order declaring that this decision violated the Applicant’s rights under sections 86 and 87(a) the CCRA; C. an order declaring that the decision violated the Applicant’s rights under section 7 of the Charter; and D. an order requiring the Respondents not to proceed with a transfer outside the Kingston area until the Applicant has accessed the health services and treatment which he currently seeks.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant's November 2015 memorandum seeks to quash transfer and prevent transfer until health services accessed.

propositions.text: Applicant failed to grieve transfer decision; proper recourse is internal grievance and judicial review of final decision.
propositions.quote: While the Applicant’s pending transfer to Stony Mountain Institution may be a relevant factor to consider in this matter, the Applicant has failed to challenge this decision through the proper channels. At the date of the hearing, counsel for the Applicant informed the Court that the Applicant had not grieved the transfer decision. The proper recourse for the Applicant is to challenge his pending transfer within the CCRA’s internal grievance process and if unsatisfied, to seek judicial review of the final decision before this Court.

propositions.text: Granting relief on transfer would circumvent exhaustion of statutory remedies and is beyond scope of this review.
propositions.quote: If this Court were to grant the relief sought in the Applicant’s Memorandum of Fact and Law, it would allow the Applicant to circumvent his obligation to exhaust his statutory remedies before bringing this matter before the Court. Moreover, the decision to transfer the Applicant out of the province to Stony Mountain Institution is based on factual and legal considerations which are beyond the scope of this application for judicial review.

propositions.text: Relief and issues remain as defined in the Notice of Application, not the memorandum.
propositions.quote: For these reasons, the relief sought and the issues to be adjudicated will remain as defined in the Notice of Application.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant failed to grieve transfer; relief on transfer would circumvent remedies; issues remain as in Notice of Application.

propositions.text: Court may decline judicial review if adequate alternative remedy exists (citing cases).
propositions.quote: It is trite law that the Court has the discretion to decline to exercise its jurisdiction to hear an application for judicial review where an adequate alternative avenue of relief remains available to an applicant (C.B. Powell Ltd. v Canada (Border Services Agency), 2010 FCA 61 at paras 31-32, [2011] 2 FCR 332; Froom v Canada (Minister of Justice), 2004 FCA 352 at para 12, [2005] 2 FCR 195).

paragraphs.summary: Court may decline judicial review if adequate alternative remedy exists, citing precedent.

propositions.text: CCRA sections 90-91 entitle offenders to fair, expeditious grievance resolution; grievance procedure in CCRR sections 74-82.
propositions.quote: Under sections 90 and 91 of the CCRA, offenders are entitled to the fair and expeditious resolution of their grievances. The grievance procedure is set forth in sections 74 to 82 of the Corrections and Conditional Release Regulations, SOR/92-620 [CCRR].

paragraphs.summary: CCRA sections 90-91 entitle offenders to fair grievance resolution; grievance procedure in CCRR sections 74-82.

propositions.text: Justice Rothstein found grievance procedure under CCRA and CCRR is an adequate alternative remedy to judicial review
propositions.quote: Justice Rothstein found that the grievance procedure set out in the CCRA and the CCRR affords an adequate alternative remedy to judicial review

propositions.text: Grievance procedure is expeditious, less costly, and allows appeal on merits unlike judicial review
propositions.quote: Grievances are to be handled expeditiously and time limits are provided in the Commissioner's Directives. There is no suggestion that the process is costly. If anything it is less costly than judicial review and more simple and straightforward

propositions.text: Judicial review does not deal with merits and only returns matter for redetermination
propositions.quote: Judicial review does not deal with the merits and a favourable result to an inmate would simply return the matter for redetermination to the tribunal appealed from

paragraphs.summary: Justice Rothstein found grievance procedure under CCRA and CCRR is an adequate, less costly alternative remedy to judicial review, which does not deal with merits.

propositions.text: This Court consistently recognizes CSC grievance process as adequate alternative remedy; judicial review appropriate only after final grievance decision
propositions.quote: This Court has consistently recognized CSC’s grievance process as an adequate alternative remedy and judicial review will generally only be appropriate after a final decision is rendered in the grievance process

paragraphs.summary: The Court finds CSC grievance process adequate and judicial review generally only after final grievance decision.

propositions.text: Policy reasons require exhaustion of internal remedies before judicial review to preserve legitimacy and timeliness
propositions.quote: The policy reasons for requiring applicants to exhaust their internal remedies are compelling. To hold otherwise is to undermine the legitimacy of alternate remedies

propositions.text: Internal remedies have primary role due to timeliness, familiarity, safeguards, and economy
propositions.quote: In the context of correctional facilities, one could identify timeliness, familiarity with a unique environment, adequate procedural safeguards and economy as reasons for which internal remedies ought to be exhausted before approaching this Court

paragraphs.summary: Justice Pelletier explained policy reasons require exhaustion of internal remedies before judicial review to preserve legitimacy and timeliness.

propositions.text: Exhausting internal remedy may resolve issue or provide court with expert final decision and complete record
propositions.quote: exhausting an internal remedy may eliminate the need for judicial review by resolving the substantive issue in favour of the griever

paragraphs.summary: Exhausting internal remedies may resolve issues or provide court with expert final decision and complete record, court states.

propositions.text: Court may exercise discretion to hear judicial review despite alternative remedy in compelling circumstances
propositions.quote: there may be circumstances where a judge may be persuaded to exercise their discretionary jurisdiction to hear the application for judicial review despite the availability of an alternative remedy

propositions.text: In Gates, judicial review allowed due to urgent health risk from cold temperatures, bypassing grievance process
propositions.quote: Justice Phelan allowed an application for judicial review where the temperature in a detention unit was repeatedly falling between O˚C and -12˚C, thus jeopardizing the Applicants’ health

propositions.text: Court intervention warranted in immediate, urgent matters without requiring grievance exhaustion
propositions.quote: He found that the matter was therefore immediate and urgent, and the Applicants were not required to exhaust their remedies through the grievance process

paragraphs.summary: Court may hear judicial review despite alternative remedy in compelling circumstances, as in Gates where urgent health risk justified bypassing grievance.

propositions.text: Court should not lightly interfere with grievance process; only in compelling cases like physical or mental harm
propositions.quote: The Court should not lightly interfere with the complaints process. There are strong policy and statutory reasons for requiring inmates to use this process

propositions.text: Issue is whether compelling circumstances justify departing from exhaustion principle
propositions.quote: the issue to be decided is whether there are compelling circumstances in this case which would justify departing from the general principle

paragraphs.summary: Court should not lightly interfere with grievance process; issue is whether compelling circumstances justify departure from exhaustion principle.

propositions.text: Applicant had not pursued grievance beyond first level when proceedings started in June 2014
propositions.quote: When the Applicant initiated these proceedings in June 2014, he had not pursued his grievance beyond the first level

propositions.text: Applicant says he was unaware of first level grievance decision until September 2015
propositions.quote: The Applicant maintains that he was not made aware of the first level grievance decision until September 2015

paragraphs.summary: Applicant had not pursued grievance beyond first level and claims he was unaware of first level decision until September 2015.

propositions.text: Applicant’s parole officer says Applicant received first level grievance response on November 21, 2013
propositions.quote: the Applicant’s parole officer at Millhaven Institution asserts that the Applicant received a response to his first level grievance on November 21, 2013

propositions.text: No record shows decision was communicated to Applicant in November 2013; transfer may explain non-communication
propositions.quote: there is no indication in the record that the decision was communicated to the Applicant in November 2013

paragraphs.summary: Parole officer says Applicant received grievance response Nov 2013, but court finds no record of communication; transfer may explain this.

propositions.text: Applicant may not have received first level grievance decision initially but this is not compelling circumstance
propositions.quote: While I accept that the Applicant may not have been provided a copy of the first level grievance decision when it was first issued, I am not persuaded that this constitutes compelling circumstances

propositions.text: Applicant partly responsible for delay by not following up with CSC authorities
propositions.quote: Applicant is in part responsible for the delay incurred before the final level grievance was initiated in failing to follow up with CSC authorities for a response

propositions.text: Applicant familiar with grievance process and actively made requests and expressed discontent with CSC officials
propositions.quote: Applicant is no stranger to the grievance process at CSC. In addition to the several grievances lodged by the Applicant on a variety of issues, the Applicant has not shown any hesitation in making countless requests with CSC officials and in expressing his discontent

paragraphs.summary: Court finds Applicant may not have received grievance decision but this is not compelling; Applicant partly responsible for delay and familiar with grievance process.

propositions.text: Important to consider nature of treatments and services requested by Applicant to assess compelling circumstances
propositions.quote: it is important to consider the nature of the treatments and services requested by the Applicant, which I will now review

paragraphs.summary: Court states it is important to consider nature of treatments requested by Applicant to assess compelling circumstances.

propositions.text: Applicant requested rhinoplasty surgery to correct nose shape, included in first and final grievances
propositions.quote: The Applicant has requested rhinoplasty surgery to correct the shape of his nose. This issue was included in both his first level and final level grievances

paragraphs.summary: Applicant requested rhinoplasty surgery included in first and final grievances.

propositions.text: Applicant underwent septoplasty on March 5, 2015, which did not include rhinoplasty
propositions.quote: On March 5, 2015, the Applicant underwent a septoplasty that he had requested to correct a deviated nasal septum. The surgery did not involve rhinoplasty

propositions.text: Surgeon Dr. Qureshy explained rhinoplasty unlikely to help glasses fit and was not recommended
propositions.quote: Dr. Qureshy... indicated that he explained to the Applicant that rhinoplasty would likely only allow the Applicant’s glasses to sit more evenly on his nose. He opined that this was not a good reason to have the rhinoplasty surgery

propositions.text: Dr. Qureshy said Applicant’s nose mildly deviated and rhinoplasty may not address main concern
propositions.quote: Applicant’s nose was only very mildly deviated and that the rhinoplasty may not even address his main concern regarding how his glasses do not sit evenly on his nose

propositions.text: Dr. Qureshy preferred glasses fit nose rather than nose fit glasses and offered second opinion
propositions.quote: he felt that it would be best to have the glasses fit the Applicant’s nose as opposed to having the Applicant’s nose fit the glasses... offered to seek another opinion

paragraphs.summary: Applicant had septoplasty; surgeon said rhinoplasty unlikely to help glasses fit and was not recommended; offered second opinion.

propositions.text: Specialist Dr. Hollins said issue cosmetic, surgery success limited, and not covered by CSC plan
propositions.quote: Dr. Hollins... advised the Applicant that his issue was essentially cosmetic... any surgical correction was likely to have a fairly limited chance of success... if cosmetic rhinoplasty was not covered under the CSC plan, the Applicant would have to pay

propositions.text: Dr. Hollins suggested glasses with adjustable nasal bridge pads to address difficulty
propositions.quote: he suggested that the Applicant be provided with glasses that have adjustable positioning of the nasal bridge pads

paragraphs.summary: Specialist said issue cosmetic, surgery unlikely successful and not covered; suggested adjustable glasses to help.

propositions.text: CSC’s National Essential Health Service Framework excludes coverage for aesthetic surgeries including external nasal deviation
propositions.quote: surgical procedures solely for aesthetic reasons, including external nasal deviation (acquired or congenital), are not covered

paragraphs.summary: CSC policy excludes coverage for aesthetic surgeries including external nasal deviation.

propositions.text: Applicant continues to request rhinoplasty and is willing to pay for it
propositions.quote: The Applicant continues to request this treatment, and is willing to pay for it

paragraphs.summary: Applicant continues to request rhinoplasty and is willing to pay for it.

propositions.text: Applicant requests full replacement of two chipped teeth with implants, included only in final grievance
propositions.quote: The Applicant requests the full replacement of two chipped teeth with implants. This request was not included in the August 2013 grievance. It was subsequently included in the September 2015 final level grievance

paragraphs.summary: Applicant requests dental implants for two chipped teeth, included only in final grievance.

propositions.text: Applicant made multiple requests to see dentist about chipped teeth in 2011 and requested meeting with Chief of Health Care in 2013
propositions.quote: Applicant made requests to see a dentist about his chipped teeth on March 22, 2011, June 12, 2011, September 19, 2011 and September 26, 2011... requested on October 2, 2013, a meeting with the Chief of Health Care Services

paragraphs.summary: Applicant made multiple requests to see dentist in 2011 and requested meeting with Chief of Health Care in 2013.

propositions.text: Parole officer says Applicant did not request dentist after transfer to Millhaven; request made after judicial review started
propositions.quote: Applicant did not request to see a dentist since his transfer to Millhaven Institution... His request was only submitted after the commencement of the application for judicial review

propositions.text: Applicant inquired about cost of implants in July 2014 and was advised procedure not possible in institution and costly
propositions.quote: Applicant made an inquiry as to the cost of replacing two teeth with implants... advised... cost would be anywhere between $3000 to $6000... procedure could not be done at any institution

paragraphs.summary: Parole officer says Applicant did not request dentist after transfer; inquired about implant cost after judicial review started and was advised procedure costly and unavailable in institution.

propositions.text: Institution dentist advised implants and orthodontics not covered by CSC and costs borne by inmate
propositions.quote: dental implants, dental implant related procedures and orthodontics do not fall under the National Essential Health Services Framework. All costs... are to be borne by the inmate

propositions.text: Dentist recommended first consultation with Dr. Nguyen to coordinate implant procedure and cost estimate
propositions.quote: recommended that the Applicant’s first consultation appointment be made with Dr. Nguyen, as she would coordinate the implant procedure

propositions.text: Applicant would be notified of costs and could submit form to cover costs if proceeding
propositions.quote: Upon receipt, the Applicant would be notified of such costs and he could then complete and submit a form to healthcare to cover the costs

paragraphs.summary: Dentist advised implants not covered by CSC; recommended consultation with Dr. Nguyen and explained cost notification and payment process.

propositions.text: Referral made for consultation with Dr. Nguyen with cost inquiry; procedure not medically necessary
propositions.quote: a referral for consultation and report was made by Dr. Erwin to Dr. Nguyen... cost of the appointment... procedure is not medically necessary

paragraphs.summary: Referral made for consultation with Dr. Nguyen with cost inquiry; procedure deemed not medically necessary.

propositions.text: Applicant has already been fitted with a dental bridge despite requesting implants
propositions.quote: Despite his request for implants, the Applicant has already been fitted with a dental bridge.

paragraphs.summary: The court states the Applicant has already been fitted with a dental bridge despite requesting implants.

propositions.text: CSC’s National Essential Health Service Framework excludes dental implants
propositions.quote: Under the terms of CSC’s National Essential Health Service Framework dated July 23, 2015, dental implants are not covered.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes CSC’s health framework excludes coverage for dental implants.

propositions.text: Applicant willing to pay for dental implants but expects compensation as injuries caused by CSC staff
propositions.quote: The Applicant is willing to pay for the requested dental implants, although he expects to be compensated because, in his view, the injuries were caused by CSC staff.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant argues he will pay for implants but expects compensation due to injuries caused by CSC staff.

propositions.text: Applicant says left hand injured during January 27, 2011 use of force incident and requests finger surgery
propositions.quote: According to the Applicant, his left hand was injured during the January 27, 2011 use of force incident. He requests surgery to repair the tendons in his left hand fifth finger.

propositions.text: Issue included in first and final level grievances
propositions.quote: This issue was included in the first and final level grievances.

propositions.text: Applicant requested healthcare for broken left pinkie finger on August 9, 2010
propositions.quote: I note upon review of the record before the Court that August 9, 2010, the Applicant made a request for healthcare for a “BROKEN left pinkie finger @ joint”.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant says his left hand was injured in 2011 and requests surgery; this was included in grievances and prior healthcare requests.

propositions.text: Several x-rays of Applicant’s left hand showed no fracture
propositions.quote: x-rays of the Applicant’s left hand were interpreted January 27, 2011, May 9, 2011 and April 17, 2012, and none of them revealed a fracture.

propositions.text: An x-ray requested July 21, 2013 results not in record
propositions.quote: An x-ray of the Applicant’s left hand was also requested on July 21, 2013; the results however do not form part of the record.

paragraphs.summary: The court finds multiple x-rays showed no fracture; a 2013 x-ray result is missing from the record.

propositions.text: September 2015 referral for left hand deferred as not urgent or life threatening
propositions.quote: On September 14, 2015, CSC staff at Millhaven Institution deferred the referral as the injury was not considered urgent or life threatening and could be followed up at the Applicant’s receiving institution.

paragraphs.summary: The court notes a 2015 referral was deferred as the injury was not urgent or life threatening.

propositions.text: Applicant requested new glasses that fit his nose, included only in final grievance
propositions.quote: The Applicant has requested a new pair of glasses that properly fit his nose. This issue was only included in his final level grievance.

propositions.text: Applicant willing to pay for new glasses expecting later compensation
propositions.quote: The Applicant is willing to pay for a new pair, again under the expectation that he will be compensated at a later date.

paragraphs.summary: The Applicant requested new glasses fitting his nose and is willing to pay, expecting compensation later.

propositions.text: CSC requires glasses to be purchased through CSC contractors
propositions.quote: The CSC maintains that the Applicant must wear glasses purchased through CSC contractors.

propositions.text: Applicant fitted with CORCAN glasses July 16, 2014 by Dr. Kogan
propositions.quote: On July 16, 2014, the Applicant was fitted with “CORCAN” glasses by Dr. Kogan, an optometrist.

propositions.text: Applicant told he must reduce personal effects to buy another pair as glasses exceed $1500 limit
propositions.quote: he was informed that he must reduce his personal effects in order to purchase another pair, as the glasses would exceed his $1500 personal effects limit.

paragraphs.summary: CSC requires glasses from contractors; Applicant was fitted with CORCAN glasses and told of personal effects limit for new glasses.

propositions.text: Specialist recommended glasses with adjustable nasal bridge pads for Applicant
propositions.quote: the specialist who was consulted with respect to the value of performing rhinoplasty surgery indicated that the Applicant should be provided with glasses that have adjustable positioning of the nasal bridge pads

propositions.text: Applicant listed with Dr. Kogan on October 28, 2015 to obtain better fitting glasses
propositions.quote: On October 28, 2015, the Applicant was listed with Dr. Kogan to obtain glasses that better fit his nose.

propositions.text: CSC permits Applicant to pay for further upgrades per guidelines
propositions.quote: CSC has also permitted the Applicant to pay for any further upgrades in accordance with CSC guidelines.

paragraphs.summary: Specialist recommended adjustable glasses; Applicant listed to get them; CSC allows payment for upgrades per guidelines.

propositions.text: Applicant argues delays due to transfers and waitlists causing inconvenience
propositions.quote: Applicant has made a compelling argument that the health treatment and services he has requested over the years have not been forthcoming because he has been transferred to four different institutions since the January 27, 2011 incident and thus finds himself at the end of waitlists, resulting in further delay and inconvenience

propositions.text: Respondents show several requests accommodated in last year
propositions.quote: Respondents have also demonstrated that several of the Applicant’s requests have been accommodated in the last year in one form or another.

paragraphs.summary: Applicant argues delays due to transfers; Respondents show several requests accommodated recently.

propositions.text: Whether final grievance process should continue given Applicant’s imminent transfer
propositions.quote: The Court is faced with the difficult decision of determining whether the final grievance process should run its course, knowing that the Applicant is facing an imminent transfer out of the province.

propositions.text: Applicant might have succeeded in preventing or delaying transfer if he had grieved it
propositions.quote: Had the Applicant initiated a grievance challenging his transfer to Manitoba, he might have succeeded in either preventing or delaying his transfer long enough to be able to access further treatment.

paragraphs.summary: Court considers if grievance process should continue given imminent transfer; notes Applicant might have delayed transfer by grieving.

propositions.text: Evidentiary record lacks proof that requested treatments are essential
propositions.quote: The evidentiary record is also lacking with respect to the “essential” nature of the assessments and treatments requested by the Applicant.

propositions.text: Section 86 CCRA requires essential healthcare conforming to professional standards
propositions.quote: section 86 of the CCRA provides that every inmate shall be provided with essential healthcare that shall conform to professionally accepted standards

propositions.text: Determination of required services relies on healthcare professionals’ judgment
propositions.quote: the determination about which service is required for an inmate must rely on the judgment of the healthcare professionals.

propositions.text: No evidence to dismiss professionals’ evaluations or that Applicant will suffer harm if waiting
propositions.quote: this Court has not been provided with any evidence to dismiss their evaluations or recommended treatment. The Court has also not been provided with any evidence regarding professionally accepted standards in the general community or any evidence that the Applicant will suffer harm, let alone irreparable harm, if he is required to wait for further consultations.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds no evidence treatments are essential or that Applicant will suffer harm if waiting; relies on professional judgment and CCRA.

propositions.text: Parole officer says Millhaven will send Healthcare Transfer Summary to receiving institution
propositions.quote: The Applicant’s parole officer has indicated that when the Applicant is transferred from Millhaven Institution to Stony Mountain Institution, Millhaven Institution will first send a “Healthcare Transfer Summary” to the receiving institution

propositions.text: If Applicant succeeds in grievances, decision will be communicated to receiving institution for action
propositions.quote: If the Applicant is successful on any of the matters he is grieving, I expect that the decision will be communicated to the receiving institution, which in turn will be required to act upon the matters identified.

paragraphs.summary: Parole officer states healthcare summary will be sent on transfer; successful grievances will be communicated for action.

propositions.text: After final grievance decision, Applicant can assess disagreements and pursue judicial review more focused
propositions.quote: When the final level grievance decision is issued, the Applicant will be in a position to assess whether there are any outstanding issues with which he is in disagreement. If he chooses to pursue the matter, his application for judicial review will likely be more focussed both factually and legally

propositions.text: Court will be better positioned to adjudicate denial of essential health services or Charter violations then
propositions.quote: the Court will then be in a better position to adjudicate whether he has been denied access to essential health services and whether his rights have been violated under the Charter.

paragraphs.summary: Court finds final grievance decision will allow focused judicial review and better adjudication of health service denial or Charter issues.

propositions.text: Application for judicial review is premature due to failure to exhaust remedies
propositions.quote: Given my finding that the application for judicial review is premature due to a failure to exhaust alternative remedies

propositions.text: No need to decide mootness or reasonableness of CSC’s response
propositions.quote: it is not necessary for me to decide whether the application for judicial review is moot or whether the CSC reasonably addressed the Applicant’s requests for treatment and health services.

paragraphs.summary: Court concludes judicial review application is premature and declines to decide mootness or CSC’s reasonableness.

propositions.text: No need to rule on Applicant’s interlocutory injunction motion after dismissal
propositions.quote: having dismissed and disposed of the application for judicial review, it is not necessary for me to rule on the Applicant’s motion for an interlocutory injunction.

paragraphs.summary: Court declines to rule on interlocutory injunction motion after dismissing application.

propositions.text: Applicant seeks costs
propositions.quote: Both the Applicant and the Respondents seek costs.

propositions.text: Respondents seek costs
propositions.quote: Both the Applicant and the Respondents seek costs.

propositions.text: No costs awarded; each party bears own costs due to circumstances
propositions.quote: I have decided, in the exercise of my discretion, that there shall be no costs. THIS COURT’S JUDGMENT is that the application for judicial review is dismissed and each party will bear their own costs.

paragraphs.summary: Both parties seek costs; court exercises discretion to award no costs and each party bears own costs.
